item.title: TT-104: Undo for TaskStore (add, complete, delete)
item.brief:
Operator request: implement backlog ticket TT-104 from BACKLOG.md in this repository exactly as its acceptance criteria state. Keep existing tests passing (`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`), add tests for what you build in a NEW file tests/test_tt104_undo.py (do not edit tests/test_basic.py), use only the standard library, and commit only this ticket on your branch. Follow the repo's CLAUDE-style rules: small functions, meaningful assertions at boundaries, no swallowed exceptions.

Ticket TT-104: Undo.
`tasktracker.store.TaskStore` has `add`, `complete` and `delete`. Add `undo()`:
- It reverts the most recent not-yet-undone `add`, `complete` or `delete`; repeated calls walk further back (LIFO), across all three kinds.
- Undoing an `add` removes that task; undoing a `complete` makes the task open again; undoing a `delete` restores the task exactly as it was, under the same id.
- Ids are never reused, even after undoing an `add`.
- With nothing left to undo, `undo()` raises `NothingToUndo` (defined in `tasktracker.store`).
- Failed operations (e.g. completing an unknown id) are not recorded.

item.title: TT-103: Search query syntax in tasktracker.search.search
item.brief:
Operator request: implement backlog ticket TT-103 from BACKLOG.md in this repository exactly as its acceptance criteria state. Keep existing tests passing (`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`), add tests for what you build in a NEW file tests/test_tt103_search.py (do not edit tests/test_basic.py), use only the standard library, and commit only this ticket on your branch. Follow the repo's CLAUDE-style rules: small functions, meaningful assertions at boundaries, no swallowed exceptions.

Ticket TT-103: Search query syntax.
`tasktracker.search.search(tasks, query)` only does a case-sensitive substring match on titles. Support a small query language instead:
- The query is split into terms on whitespace, except inside double quotes: `"fix login"` is one phrase term. All terms must match (AND).
- A bare word or phrase matches when it appears in the title, case-insensitively.
- `tag:NAME` matches tasks that have the tag NAME (exact tag, case-insensitive).
- `status:open` / `status:done` match on status.
- Any other `field:value` term, an unknown status, or an unterminated quote raises `QueryError` (defined in `tasktracker.search`).
- An empty or blank query matches every task. Results keep the input order.

item.title: TT-102: RFC 4180 CSV export in tasktracker.export.to_csv
item.brief:

Keep existing tests passing (`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`), add tests for what you build in a NEW file tests/test_tt102_csv.py (do not edit tests/test_basic.py), use only the standard library, and commit only this ticket on your branch. Follow the repo's CLAUDE-style rules: small functions, meaningful assertions at boundaries, no swallowed exceptions.

Ticket TT-102: RFC 4180 CSV export.
`tasktracker.export.to_csv(tasks)` joins fields with commas and breaks on titles containing commas, quotes or newlines. It must produce RFC 4180 CSV:
- Header `id,title,tags,status,due`; one row per task in the given order.
- Tags joined with `;`, due date as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` or empty.
- A field containing a comma, double quote, CR or LF is wrapped in double quotes, with embedded double quotes doubled. Other fields are not quoted.
- Every line (header included) ends with CRLF.

item.title: TT-101: Reject impossible due dates in tasktracker.dates.parse_due
item.brief:
Operator request: implement backlog ticket TT-101 from BACKLOG.md in this repository exactly as its acceptance criteria state. Keep existing tests passing (`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`), add tests for what you build in a NEW file tests/test_tt101_due_dates.py (do not edit tests/test_basic.py), use only the standard library, and commit only this ticket on your branch. Follow the repo's CLAUDE-style rules: small functions, meaningful assertions at boundaries, no swallowed exceptions.

Ticket TT-101: Reject impossible due dates.
`tasktracker.dates.parse_due(text, today)` silently clamps impossible dates: `2026-02-30` becomes `2026-02-28`. Instead:
- An impossible calendar date (`2026-02-30`, `2025-02-29`, `2026-04-31`, `2026-13-01`, `2026-00-10`) raises `InvalidDate`, a `ValueError` subclass defined in `tasktracker.dates`, whose message contains the original text.
- Anything else that does not match a supported form also raises `InvalidDate` (today it raises a bare `ValueError`).
- Relative offsets: `+Nd` is N days after `today`, `+0d` is `today`. Negative or unsigned offsets (`-3d`, `3d`) raise `InvalidDate`.
- `today` and `tomorrow` keep working; matching stays case-insensitive and ignores surrounding whitespace.

TT-101 implemented and committed on archon/ksdpepdp-tt-101-reject-impossible-due-dates-in-ta as fdb00ef (on f2f7893). parse_due no longer clamps: impossible calendar dates (2026-02-30, 2025-02-29, 2026-04-31, 2026-13-01, 2026-00-10) raise InvalidDate (a ValueError subclass in tasktracker.dates) with the original text in the message. Unsupported forms, and -3d / 3d, also raise InvalidDate. +Nd and +0d work, as do today/tomorrow (case-insensitive, trimmed). Offsets or tomorrow past date range raise InvalidDate. pr.body: Approach: parse_due validates the ISO date with date() and wraps its ValueError as InvalidDate (chained with `from`). Offset and tomorrow arithmetic go through _add_days, which maps OverflowError to InvalidDate. Unsupported text raises InvalidDate. ISO and offset regexes now use [0-9] instead of \d, so Unicode digits are rejected. Key files: tasktracker/dates.py, tests/test_tt101_due_dates.py (new). tests/test_basic.py is unchanged. Checks: unittest suite 14/14 OK. Review: one reviewer, pass, no blocking findings. Assumptions: an out-of-range offset counts as an unsupported date and raises InvalidDate. Open, non-blocking: offsets with more than 4300 digits raise plain ValueError from int() (Python digit limit).
pr.summary: made parse_due stop clamping bad dates. now raises InvalidDate for impossible dates, unsupported forms, and negative or unsigned offsets. before: 2026-02-30 -> 2026-02-28, -3d raised bare ValueError; now: InvalidDate for both.
pr.title: TT-101: reject impossible and unsupported due dates

risk.why: One pure function in tasktracker/dates.py changed, plus a new test file. Behaviour changes only for inputs that were previously clamped or raised bare ValueError. No persistence, security, concurrency or API break; the only caller, tests/test_basic.py, passes unchanged. Reviewer confirmed low.
